testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the driving test, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not need to brake or shift gears while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before you check the engine compartment, engage the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before you get in the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a rear-end crash and makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Driving faster can make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What maneuver might be asked of you during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What should you do if the air pressure warning light comes on?

options.text: Use one foot on the gas and one foot on the brake.
Safely leave the roadway and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the roadway and stop.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, you must stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight uphill slope.
The vehicle is on a slight downhill slope.

questions.explanation: If a trailer is attached, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If you press and release the brake pedal too often, air leaves faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure gets too low, the brakes will not work.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more. It is hard to stop or turn on slippery surfaces, so adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: When backing, a helper:

options.text: Should only be used if the driver is not confident.
Would likely get in the way.

questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper whenever you can to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: After cargo is secured, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check it for the entire trip.
You can drive at least eight hours without checking it.
Check it every three hours or 150 miles.
You should never check it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it every three hours or 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the maximum height allowed for vehicles on Illinois highways?
questions.explanation: In Illinois, vehicles cannot be taller than 13 feet, 6 inches. Height is measured from the ground to the top of the vehicle, including any load.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated on a vehicle with air brakes, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Pushing the pedal combined with the spring brakes can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, look toward the right side of the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The vehicle is easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose contact with the road and slide on a layer of water instead.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with engine belts?

options.text: Inspect them only if they look frayed.
Leave them alone and do not inspect them.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check all engine belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people not paying attention to the road, such as construction workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road. Someone sitting safely on a bench is not a concern.

questions.question: Water and oil can build up in air brake systems. What should be done about them?

options.text: They are necessary for the air brake system to work properly.
They should be added if low.

questions.explanation: Water and oil build up in air brake systems and can damage the brakes. You must drain the air tanks daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify you from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years, including kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban. Speeding does not disqualify you.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, how often should it be checked?

options.text: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
Only after arriving at the final destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and after the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo secure throughout the trip.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Never try to outrun an approaching train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to outrun an approaching train.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming, and signals may not warn you. Never try to outrun a train at a railroad crossing.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: Which braking system uses the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is used when you press the brake pedal to slow down or stop your vehicle during normal driving.

questions.question: How much water on a road causes hydroplaning?

options.text: A good amount, such as a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Slowly build up pressure over a few minutes.
Come up to a normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then decrease quickly while the engine runs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come up to a normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach a normal level in a few seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: What is the name for a thin layer of ice on roads?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on roads. You can see the road surface through it, so it may look like wet pavement. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to keep it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: What should you do during the on-road driving test?

options.text: Develop your own route to show off your driving skills.
Listen to directions from the examiner.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to directions from the examiner.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, listen to and follow the examiner's directions. They will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, it should be:
questions.explanation: Check that all parts of the exhaust system are secure. No parts should be loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check the hoses for?

options.text: To ensure that they are still clear.
To ensure that they are connected to the battery.
For the proper amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level for any signs of leaks.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, increase the distance between you and the vehicle in front. This gives the tailgater room to pass safely. Speeding up may not help because they may tailgate you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: Why should flares be used with caution after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.
Other drivers may get confused about what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Spilled fuel can ignite if flares are not used carefully. This can cause a fire at the accident scene.

questions.question: Which statement about wheels is correct?

options.text: A rim with one missing lug nut is safe if it has four other lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded wheel repairs are safe on rear axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous defects. Bent or cracked lock rings are not safe. Welded wheel repairs are not safe.

questions.question: While driving downhill, brake until your speed is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake.
questions.explanation: Brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this process as you go downhill.

questions.question: What can reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can lead to aggressive driving, which is dangerous. Calming music can help you relax and reduce stress while driving.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Use them only when there is traffic.
Check them regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: You need to be aware of everything around you. Check your mirrors often to see what is behind and beside you.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave space open on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave space open on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, keep your rear close to the curb. Leaving space on your right side can confuse other drivers. They may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: What is the benefit of a vehicle inspection?

options.text: It is a waste of time.
It finds small problems before they become big ones.
Drivers should not do it themselves.
It must be done once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: It finds small problems before they become big ones.
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle before each trip. This helps catch small problems before they become serious. It is better to find a problem at home than on the road.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, pressing the brake pedal causes air pressure to push out the rod and move the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What happens if a CMV driver refuses a chemical test when an officer asks?

options.text: The driver's license is suspended for two months.
The driver's license is suspended for 12 months.
The driver is told to drive straight home.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver's license is suspended for 12 months.
questions.explanation: Any driver who refuses a chemical test will have their license suspended for at least 12 months. This applies to all drivers, not just CMV drivers.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need ____ to shift gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to shift gears. This technique takes practice to master.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, air pressure of at least ____ should be built up in both braking systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving, let the air compressor build up 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed only on the left side, if possible.
Placed only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. Placing weight too high increases the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Have air pressure in the braking system even when the vehicle is not running.
Keep some air pressure in the braking system when the vehicle is not running.
Must run to build air pressure for the brakes to work properly.
Keep air pressure when shut off for less than four hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run to build air pressure for the brakes to work properly.
questions.explanation: Before driving, let the air compressor build up 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: If a driver operates in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license type should they choose?
questions.explanation: To operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must choose a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep downgrade:

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking effect.
questions.explanation: Use engine braking as your main way to control speed on a downgrade. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when needed for extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: If a vehicle gets stuck on a railroad track, the driver should:

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out and walk away from the tracks.
Try to flag down another vehicle for a push.
Wait in the vehicle for police to arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: Exit the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: Air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by vehicle speed, vehicle weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.
